item.title: splitkey: Three Ways to Own a Vanity Address That the Seller Cannot Touch
item.description:
Every vanity address has the same problem. It is found by brute force, so somebody knows the private key. The question is not “is the seller honest today?”. The question is “what can a copy of that key do tomorrow?”.

I made splitkey.me to answer that question in public, with one rule: every claim must be checkable on-chain, by you, without us.

item.title: scomp-mcp: Letting an AI Agent Use a Terminal on a Host It Cannot Reach
item.description:
I have a GPU host in a private network. It has no public IP and no SSH access from my laptop. I also have an AI coding agent on my laptop. The agent is good at builds and benchmarks, but it cannot reach that host.

The scomp agent already connects that host to the scomp relay with an outbound connection. So the missing part was small: a tool that lets a local model use the same terminal sessions, under the same rules. That tool is scomp-mcp.

item.title: scomp-agent: My tmux Sessions on the Phone, Without SSH and Without Open Ports
item.description:
I start long jobs in tmux. Then I go away from the laptop. Then I want to know if the job is finished. For many years, my procedure was this: find a laptop, connect a VPN, open SSH, attach to tmux, and read one line. That is five steps to read one line.

The phone is always in my pocket. The terminal session is always on a server. I wrote scomp to connect these two things. This post is about scomp-agent, the small Go binary that runs next to your sessions.

item.title: The Quest for a Secure Wi-Fi AP on Linux (Realtek Edition)
item.description:
I recently set out to turn my ThinkCentre into a high-security wireless access point. My goal was simple: spin up a dedicated AP for my VR setup using modern WPA3-SAE security.

The hardware? A Realtek RTL8822CE. The result? A lesson in Linux driver limitations.

If you are trying to force WPA3 on a Realtek card and seeing supplicant-timeout errors, this guide is for you. Here is how I hit the wall, and the “Maximum Security” WPA2 configuration I used to fix it while staying FIPS-compliant.
